issue: observed_at is a batch/write-time stamp, not a per-fetch time. In verification.jsonl all 70 checks of each verifier share one timestamp (verifier-A 2026-11-14T22:20:52Z, verifier-B 22:18:50Z, verifier-C 22:20:00Z); all 24 provenance records share 22:27:25Z, which equals provenance.jsonl's file mtime (01:27:25 +03). Discovery researched_at is '2026-11-15T12:00:00Z' for all 30 records, about 13.5 h AFTER the files were written (mtimes 01:17-01:21 +03 on 2026-11-15 = 22:17-22:21Z on 14 Nov). pilot_harness check_evidence() uses observed_at as the only freshness signal, so the 45-day freshness gate is satisfied by construction and says nothing about when a page was actually seen.
recommended_fix: Require per-check observed_at captured at fetch time (or drop it and require the fetch log id); reject records where >N checks share an identical second; reject researched_at/observed_at in the future relative to the run clock; add a unit test for both.
limitations: Inference from timestamps and file mtimes (stat). Original verification_A/B/C shard files were not present, so shard write times were not stat-able; the merged file's mtime (22:21:07Z) is consistent with the shard stamps.

issue: State/official sources dominate the proposed RADAR tier and cannot be reconciled with the acceptance policy. 7 of 20 proposed RADAR sources are state or government channels (SANA K003, IRNA K047, AZERTAC K070, TASS K083, Xinhua K132, Turkish MFA K159, EC Press Corner K105). Verifiers FAILed originality for 6 of them (K003 K070 K083 K105 K132 K159; K047 UNKNOWN) yet gave PASS on provenance and, for K003/K070/K083/K105/K159, PASS on perspective. pilot_policy needs >=27 originality PASS, so the best case with these 6 failing is 24: the gate is unreachable as designed, which creates pressure to reclassify 'official primary' as 'original'. Re-fetch confirms the character of the output: TASS item 2218193 is entirely a relay of a Facebook post by PM Radev; Xinhua 14 Nov item has MOFCOM as sole origin and no US-side voice; AZERTAC calls itself 'the sole source of official government news'; SANA reports a six-killed toll with no named origin.
recommended_fix: Add a separate OFFICIAL_POSITION lane (flag state_affiliation=true) that is excluded from 'accepted original source' and 'independent corroboration' counts; set min_verified_originality over non-state sources only or remove state/official sources from the 27-of-30 denominator; forbid state outlets as sole or corroborating evidence on factual claims; rename 'provenance PASS' for these to ORIGIN_CLASS_IDENTIFIED.
limitations: Tier labels are the harness's proposed_tier (legacy-derived), not editorial decisions. Policy arithmetic assumes the 6 FAILs stand.

issue: Same-evidence-family corroboration passes the gate today. provenance_edges.json in the repo is an empty list ([]), so none of the 24 edges in provenance.jsonl affect independent_families(). Concretely: (a) Nasser Hospital strike 12-13 Nov: Xinhua (K132), TASS (K083) and SANA (K003) all rest on Gaza health authorities/IDF/Turkish MFA statements and TASS-Xinhua have a 2026-2030 content-sharing agreement; (b) Peskov's APEC statement appears via TASS (K083) and Naftemporiki (K029, credited 'ΑΠΕ-ΜΠΕ, με πληροφορίες από Reuters') - one origin; (c) Haaretz's anonymous-sourced UAE-warning story reaches Al-Monitor (K065) as AFP copy. Each pair carries a different provenance_family string, so independent_families() returns 2-3. Re-fetch confirms the SANA/MFA identity (SANA reports the Turkish MFA statement posted on X; toll unattributed) and the Naftemporiki credit line.
recommended_fix: Ingest provenance.jsonl claim edges into provenance_edges.json before any readiness run; fail the gate if edges is empty while claims exist; add a regression test with TASS+Xinhua on the same claim_id expecting 1 independent family.
limitations: Edges are as recorded by the provenance auditor; most wire originals (Reuters/AP) were not opened by that auditor. No claims.json entries cite these claims yet, so the harm is latent.

issue: Gate logic can undercount dependence and accept 'unknown' provenance. (1) independent_families() only merges edges whose relationship is in CLAIM_DEPENDENT_RELATIONSHIPS and whose BOTH endpoints are pilot sources with a family string; source-level 'partnership' edges (TASS-Xinhua K083-K132; Naftemporiki-CMG) and every edge touching an EXT: node (AFP, Axios, Glasnaya, Planet-WaPo, Sky News) are ignored. (2) source_readiness() rejects provenance_family only if it equals exactly 'UNKNOWN'; provenance_families.json holds 'UNKNOWN (own-field-reporting:K001 unconfirmed)' for K001 and 'own-field-reporting:K153 (unconfirmed)'-style strings, which pass. (3) Singleton families named after the source ('own-field-reporting:K0xx') make each source independent of every other by construction.
recommended_fix: Normalise family via startswith('UNKNOWN') or an enum; treat '(unconfirmed)' as UNKNOWN; model EXT: nodes as families so wire/upstream edges merge; add source-level partnership edges to a separate 'ownership/feed-share' penalty; add tests for each case.
limitations: Static reading of code at the current branch; no mutation of repo files was performed to demonstrate the bypass.

issue: 'provenance PASS' is awarded without upstream tracing, inflating min_verified_provenance. Verifier's own limitation fields: K105 'No item inspected.'; K123 'Source citations inside the PDF were not examined.'; K007 'Source data underlying the 416-operation count not seen.'; K244 'Citations inside pieces not examined.'; K031 'Underlying sources of analysis not seen.' The provenance auditor independently marks K031 (text in unread PDF), K007, K123, K244, K105 as unresolved. Spot-check of K031's cited explainer shows it cites no external sources at all. 19 of 30 sources carry provenance PASS, but only 5 sources (K031 K080 K112 K238 N001) pass all five mandatory checks.
recommended_fix: Redefine provenance PASS = at least one concrete item traced to a named upstream with URL (or explicit 'first-hand'); otherwise UNKNOWN. Downgrade the 14 PASSes whose limitation says the upstream was not seen.
limitations: Counts are from verification.jsonl statuses (PASS 19, UNKNOWN 11). Whether upstream exists in the unread PDFs is unknown.

issue: Mada Masr is proposed for RADAR but is operationally compromised and unverifiable. New Cairo Misdemeanour Court ordered closure and confiscation of equipment on 27 Oct 2026 (Art. 105, 2018 media law), EGP 3m fine on EiC Lina Attalah; Business Day/AFP (10 Nov) says it 'closed its newsroom while it awaits an appeal'; site blocked inside Egypt since 2017. Al Jazeera gives no appeal deadline and no statement on site availability or mirrors; the 11 Nov hearing was a separate retrial of Attalah's 2024 in-absentia sentence (outcome not reported in sources found). madamasr.com/en returned undated headlines from years past (stale cache), the 27 Oct article URL failed to load, so canonical liveness, activity and originality are all unobservable. Verifier correctly left UNKNOWN; the risk is a RADAR proposal and 'special-use' framing for a source that may stop publishing.
recommended_fix: Move K039 to HOLD (continuity risk); add a continuity check (latest dated own article on the canonical domain or a documented mirror/Substack/Telegram channel with first-party proof); record court status with dated sources; do not auto-activate.
limitations: Real appeal dates for the closure order were not found in any source read; mirror/alternate-domain existence is UNKNOWN (not found, not disproved). Found via WebFetch summaries.

issue: Meduza's only listed 'original work example' is a Glasnaya republication. The verification record for K086 lists meduza.io/feature/2026/11/14/ranshe-vrachi-... with why_original 'Republished Glasnaya reporting (not Meduza's own)'. The gate's original_work_examples test only checks is_url and is_date, so a partner republication satisfies 'dated original example'. The verifier marked originality UNKNOWN, but the record would pass the example check; provenance edge confirms Meduza and Glasnaya are one evidence chain.
recommended_fix: Require original_work_examples[*].own_work=true with a bylined/organisation-credit check; reject items whose credit line names another outlet; require at least 2 own examples.
limitations: Only one Meduza item was inspected by verification; Meduza has plenty of own reporting not examined here.

issue: Legal-pressure context under-documented in the record and perspective PASS is thin. Meduza's about page confirms foreign agent (Apr 2021), undesirable organisation (Jan 2023), Latvian SIA 'Medusa Project', donor funding, blocked in Russia, and mirror sites. Additional dated facts not in the verification record: publisher Galina Timchenko sentenced to 5 years in absentia (Dec 2025); EiC Ivan Kolpakov subject of an Interior Ministry arrest warrant (reported 17 Mar 2026); participation/donations criminalised. Verifier perspective PASS observation is one line ('Exile outlet outlawed in Russia...') with limitation 'Editorial stance beyond this not documented' - legal status is not a perspective statement. Also the discovery X handle @meduza_en is the English account; meduza.io/en meta tags name @meduzaproject as the site account (Russian flagship) - handle ownership of the two accounts not documented.
recommended_fix: Record perspective as 'exile, independent, Russian-state-designated undesirable' with dated legal events; keep both handles; flag that readers/donors in Russia face criminal liability (editorial duty-of-care note).
limitations: Moscow Times pages read via summariser; Timchenko sentence taken from the Moscow Times URL title/search listing and the March article text; did not open the Dec 2025 piece itself.

issue: IranWire is proposed RADAR with 7/7 checks UNKNOWN and an undocumented security incident. dpa/CIO (1 Apr 2026) reports the site unreachable with a maintenance notice after a claimed hack of correspondence/informant data (claimed by Iranian judiciary outlet Misan, attributed to 'Handala'); the verifier's fetch failures ('client_error') were never reconciled with this. Re-fetch of iranwire.com/en/ now returned undated excerpts only. Discovery cites en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IranWire for ownership but that URL serves Maziar Bahari's biography (funding mention is only that the original site build was USAID-funded via Small Media). Perspective 'opposition/exile' is asserted without a first-party statement.
recommended_fix: HOLD; add a data-breach/continuity risk flag; require one dated, fetched IranWire article and a first-party about page before any tier; replace the Wikipedia pointer with a first-party ownership page or mark UNKNOWN.
limitations: Hack claims are the Iranian judiciary's own via dpa; IranWire's response not found. Not evidence the site is unreliable.

issue: Haaretz: all 7 checks UNKNOWN (robots_disallowed on article pages; paywall), RADAR proposed, and the one traced story is a single anonymous-sourced origin copied downstream. Provenance auditor shows the UAE-warning story (Haaretz, 8 Sep 2026) rests on anonymous sources; Al-Monitor (K065) carries it as AFP copy that 'does not independently verify'; The National and Yeni Safak also relay. Haaretz original URL was never captured. Re-fetch of a cited haaretz.com article URL returned robots_disallowed. Ownership (Schocken 75% / Nevzlin 25%) is Wikipedia-only.
recommended_fix: HOLD until a dated Hebrew/English original is opened (e.g., via haaretz.co.il or syndicated/archived copy with provenance); do not count Al-Monitor or any outlet citing Haaretz as a second confirmation.
limitations: Paywall/robots blocks are an access limitation, not a quality judgement. Netanyahu's reported suit against Haaretz appears only as a title in discovery (not read).

issue: Discovery and verifier disagree on K153 canonical_url and the verifier's PASS overstates what was seen. Discovery: homepage stale (Nov 2024 content), article fetches blocked. Verifier: PASS from the about page. Re-fetch: addisstandard.com returns Sept/Nov 2024 content with no domain or date; the domain itself looks right (the Telegram mirror t.me/s/AddisstandardEng links to addisstandard.com/?p=578xx; NED announced Addis Standard as a 2026 Democracy Award recipient on 22 Jun 2026), but no article page on the domain loaded and none is dated after the check window. So the PASS is defensible only as 'domain identity', not 'current URL' that the policy's min_verified_url counts. Languages also disagree (discovery ['en'], verifier en/am/om per about page; verifier is right). Telegram feed mixes own articles with links to X, Facebook, AP and MEE posts - repost ratio is high and unmeasured.
recommended_fix: Downgrade canonical_url to UNKNOWN until one dated article page on addisstandard.com is opened (or a Wayback capture); record NED award as perspective/funding context only if a NED grant listing is found (the award page itself does not state grant funding).
limitations: NED award is an honour; the page read does not state NED grants fund the outlet - do not infer funding. Telegram post dates not shown (times only).

issue: K154 canonical_url PASS rests on an undated, domain-less homepage excerpt; discovery recorded fetch_blocked/dates_unverified. Re-fetch of sudantribune.com returned six 'Editors Picks' headlines with no URL, domain, timestamp (one headline: 'UN confirms 80 dead in Abyei drone strikes'); article URL sudantribune.com/?p=320989 failed to load. Search listings show pages titled 'Saturday, November 7, 2026' and 'Tuesday, October 27, 2026' on sudantribune.com, so the domain is probably live, but nothing opened confirms it. The only article opened by the verifier is dated Dec 2025. Note the Abyei strike story that Sudan Tribune headlines is the same event Reuters (K168) reported with 150+ feared dead, while the Tribune headline says 80 dead: casualty-figure conflict not examined. Owner/funder not named on about page; Paris-based.
recommended_fix: Set canonical_url UNKNOWN until a dated article page loads on the domain; compare Abyei casualty figures across K154/K168 and flag as contested.
limitations: Search-result titles are not page opens; the 80-vs-150 difference may reflect different dates (UN confirmed vs initial claim).

issue: FDD: three PASSes are weaker than recorded and funding/COI is not first-party documented. Activity PASS rests on link text 'Overnight Brief' dated 12 Nov (the brief URL failed to load for both the verifier and this audit; fdd.org/about also failed). Originality PASS cites an op-ed dated 1 Sep 2026 (75 days old, outside the policy's 45-day window), co-authored with a summer intern, no cited sources, and the page as fetched is attributed to The Washington Times - so fdd.org may be the republisher, not the originator (provenance edge direction is the opposite). Documented context (third-party): Al Jazeera, citing Carnegie, says FDD traces to 2001 donor-incorporated EMET and that a founder described the aim as 'to enhance Israel's image in North America'; FDD Action spent $150,000 lobbying in Q1 2025 per Senate filings; FDD's site states it accepts no foreign-government funding; CEO quoted 'Guilty as charged' on being called the executing arm of US Iran policy. Donor list not found first-party.
recommended_fix: Downgrade activity/originality to UNKNOWN until a dated item inside 45 days that fdd.org originates is opened; record perspective as 'advocacy think tank' with Al Jazeera/Carnegie as dated third-party context; EVENT use only with a mandatory labelled-advocacy note.
limitations: Al Jazeera article is the only source read for funding/founding claims; Carnegie, JTA, LobeLog, Prospect pieces named in discovery were NOT read. No accusation is made about donors beyond what Al Jazeera attributes.

issue: RUSI funding and COI are not established; verifier ownership PASS rests on charity registration only. RUSI's funding page (as fetched) lists funding bands (GBP 1,000 to 1,000,000+) but names no funders and says RUSI 'receives no core government funding' while income comes from 'private and governmental' sources; discovery instead lists US State Dept, UK FCDO, European Commission and BAE Systems as major contributors - sourced to Wikipedia, not to RUSI. The sampled taskforce report (13 Nov 2026) states no funder for the taskforce and is built on UK government/NCA/FCA/FATF publications about a UK government evaluation. Dependence on UK government sources and possible government funding of that very work is a COI to disclose.
recommended_fix: Mark ownership/funding PARTIAL (charity confirmed; funders UNKNOWN); require per-publication funding line; do not repeat Wikipedia donor names in the registry without first-party proof.
limitations: My fetch of the funding page may have missed a donor table rendered client-side; the summariser said none were named.

issue: SWP is state-funded and the record's perspective PASS is generous. SWP's own funding page: federal grant EUR 18.9M in 2025 (via Federal Chancellery; Bundestag-approved) covering 100% of core activities, external funding EUR 3.87M; 'does not accept any research commissions' is a self-claim. Verifier perspective PASS (SWP advises Bundestag/government; states independence) records closeness to government, which is context, not evidence of editorial independence either way. Originality PASS relies on an abstract only (SWP-Studie 2026/S 16 not read in full).
recommended_fix: Tag 'government-funded, advisory to German government' as structured perspective; keep independence as self-claim.
limitations: Low severity because funding is transparently disclosed and the PASS evidence re-fetched correctly.

issue: Omran: originality PASS evidence is stale, funding unnamed, and perspective claims conflict. The originality example is dated 2026-06-02 (166 days before the audit date; policy window 45 days) and activity is UNKNOWN. Omran's own about page says it is 'independent', 'does not adopt partisan positions', HQ Damascus, and is 'the policy research program of the Syrian Forum' but names no funders; Syrian Forum USA's page describes Omran as a program that aims to 'boost relevance and awareness of the Syrian cause', is a donation-funded 501(c)(3), and claims 190 meetings with Syrian government entities in 2025. Legacy domain omranstudies.org vs omrandirasat.org both live; discovery noted an earlier Istanbul location. Identity UNKNOWN (no own about page read by verifier).
recommended_fix: Treat perspective as 'Syrian-cause advocacy-affiliated research programme' (evidenced), funders UNKNOWN; set originality PASS aside until a dated item inside 45 days is opened; resolve which domain is canonical.
limitations: Wikipedia page for Omran was not fetchable; funding of Syrian Forum itself not investigated.

issue: Ukrainian Prism: sampled 'recent' item is a derivative of another institution's brief and the site discloses US government support. The 10 Nov 2026 piece 'When the Guns Fall Silent: Ukraine After the War' is by Oleksandr Kraiev with Andreas Umland and is based on their EPIK Policy Brief of 28 Apr 2026 (so activity PASS shows site publication, not new research). Site footer: developed with support of the Public Affairs Section of the US Embassy in Ukraine (views 'do not necessarily reflect' US government). Identity UNKNOWN (about pages unreadable); footer (c)2016. Discovery adds IRF/FES/KAS funding and a 2021 report for the Ukrainian MFA (sourced to site pages, not re-read). Perspective: single national, Euro-Atlantic view, not self-labelled.
recommended_fix: Record funder disclosure (US Embassy PAS) as structured ownership_or_funding; treat derivative republications as non-original; keep identity UNKNOWN until a legal/about page is read.
limitations: Only one item re-fetched. Donor claims beyond the footer come from discovery, unverified here.

issue: Al-Monitor: ownership undisclosed, content partly wire/relay, and the verifier's provenance PASS rests on a paywalled, undated article. Re-fetch: the Mossad-visit article is labelled SUBSCRIBER EXCLUSIVE with only the opening portion visible and no publication date; it attributes the visit detail to Axios (three unnamed sources) and the rest to unnamed Israeli political sources - verifier PASS cannot be confirmed from the truncated text. Al-Monitor's about page names only founder Jamal Daniel (2012) and 'AL-MONITOR, LLC' - no owners or investors; Wikipedia adds only a 2018 North Base Media management partnership (no equity stated). AFP copy appears in 'Originals' (6 Nov and 8 Sep items per provenance audit).
recommended_fix: Mark provenance UNKNOWN for paywalled items; require a free-access or archived full text; label ownership 'UNKNOWN beyond founder/LLC'; report Originals' wire share before RADAR.
limitations: A 2017-era Tablet critique cited by discovery was not read and is not relied on. Ownership gaps are gaps, not evidence of concealment.

issue: CRS and Reuters/Hindu are 'verified' via third-party copies or not at all, while canonical_url is BLOCKED. K123: congress.gov/crs-products robots_disallowed (re-confirmed); activity/originality/provenance PASS rest on everycrsreport.com mirror of IF13217 v4 (14 Oct 2026) - the mirror content matches (title, authors Harris/Cho, CRS disclaimer) but no footnotes are visible, and the page does not say it is official. K168: reuters.com SITE_BLOCKED (re-confirmed); activity/originality/provenance PASS rest on a TimesLive syndicated copy (re-fetch confirms Reuters byline Eltahir/Abdelaziz, 20 Oct 2026, anonymous diplomats plus Abyei information minister, 'could not immediately verify'). K138 The Hindu: SITE_BLOCKED, all checks BLOCKED/UNKNOWN. Counting a mirror/copy as the source verifies the copy, not the publisher's current canonical channel.
recommended_fix: Record verification_channel (primary|mirror|syndicated copy) per PASS; cap sources verified only via mirror at PARTIAL; run a second fetch route (browser/Wayback) for blocked domains before any tier.
limitations: BLOCKED here is an environment limit (proxy/robots), not a judgement on the sites. IRNA en.irna.ir did load for this audit but showed undated excerpts (possible stale cache) - verifier's UNKNOWN stands.

issue: English/Western/institutional over-weighting and local-language blind spots. The 30 records list English for 28/30 (inventory view); 11 are English-only (K004 K020 K065 K105 K238 K123 K244 K138 K168 N001 N002); only K029 (el) and K047 (fa) are non-English-only. Haaretz (K020) is recorded as en-only although discovery lists Hebrew; Syria Direct as en-only although it also publishes Arabic. 13 raw language codes; region labels = 11 but 'Kuresel' covers 3 sources and 'Turkiye' is 1 source that is the government itself (MFA) - there is no Turkish-language press source in a pilot built for a Turkish-language bulletin. Verification actually READ non-English page text for only: Greek (K029, K031), Russian/Armenian (K086, K077), Chinese (K132), German (K112); Persian, Hebrew, Ukrainian, Azerbaijani, Amharic/Oromo primary text was not read (IRNA/IranWire/Haaretz blocked; K225/K070 read in English). The only 5 sources passing all five mandatory checks (K031 K080 K112 K238 N001) are 3 European think tanks, one English-language Caucasus outlet and one global OSINT group - nothing from Africa, South/East Asia, Middle East or Russia. No Latin America, South Asia (The Hindu blocked), Southeast Asia, or Francophone/Sahel Africa source exists in the pilot. Missing critical local-language voices (suggestions only; NOT added to the registry and not verified): Hebrew - Kan, Ynet, Maariv; Persian - BBC Persian, Radio Farda; Turkish independent - Medyascope, bianet, T24; Ukrainian - Ukrainska Pravda, Suspilne; Russian independent - Novaya Gazeta Europe, Mediazona; Arabic - Al-Araby Al-Jadeed, Syria TV; Sudan/Horn - Dabanga, Hiiraan Online; Francophone Africa - Jeune Afrique; Latin America - Folha, El Pais America, Infobae; China - Caixin, SCMP; South Asia - Dawn, Indian Express, Scroll.
recommended_fix: Add region taxonomy (continents/sub-regions; drop 'Kuresel' and single-country 'Turkiye' from the region count); add min non-English-primary-text-read count; require at least one non-state, local-language source per region before GO; evaluate the suggested names in a separate scouting task.
limitations: Language lists come from inventory/discovery metadata and are only as good as those; 'read' is judged from verifier observations (English URL paths indicate English editions). Suggested outlets are not vetted and may carry their own state/ownership issues.

issue: ACLED is a derivative coding layer and its originality/provenance cannot be assigned from the record. ACLED's sourcing page lists four input types - traditional media (named examples include Reuters), reports from institutions/NGOs and, 'under certain conditions', conflict parties' own reports (ministries of defence, armed groups, NATO), local partner data, and selectively verified new media - and says conflict-party fatality figures are flagged less reliable. Therefore ACLED rows can embed the same Reuters/state-agency items that other pilot members carry (K168 K083 K132), and fatality fields can be conflict-party claims. Verifier: provenance UNKNOWN, activity UNKNOWN, originality PASS on listing entries of monthly overviews (6 Jul 2026 = 132 days old). ACLED's about page names UN CRAF'd as a funder; no donor list.
recommended_fix: Treat ACLED as 'coded aggregation of media/partner reports' - require per-event source field before counting an ACLED row as independent of any media source; downgrade originality to 'dataset product' not 'field reporting'.
limitations: I read the general sourcing page only; Israel/Palestine and Ethiopia sourcing pages named in search were not read. No evidence ACLED rows were actually used downstream of pilot sources.

issue: Bellingcat: OSINT label needs per-claim tagging. Re-fetch of the 5 Nov 2026 piece confirms mixed sourcing: own geolocation (DVIDS photo vs Google imagery, Bing views) but damage imagery comes from Planet via The Washington Post and from Iranian state-affiliated outlets Tasnim and Fars, and the Strava finding is Sky News's investigation (Bellingcat links to it). Verifier recorded these caveats correctly; the risk is that a downstream claim cites Bellingcat as independent confirmation of an Iranian-state-published image. Also the 6 Oct 2026 Form 990 article (40 days old) is own-document analysis.
recommended_fix: Add imagery_provider and imagery_publisher fields to claim evidence so same_imagery edges are mandatory when a Bellingcat claim uses Tasnim/Fars/WaPo imagery.
limitations: Bellingcat funding not investigated in this audit.

issue: Hetq: tier rationale (investigative) is not supported by the sampled item. Article 185453 (14 Nov 2026 12:30) is a three-author retrospective ('history of National Assembly brawls') with an embedded YouTube video and no cited sources; verifier correctly left originality/provenance UNKNOWN but activity PASS counts it. About page shows Gulbenkian Foundation logo and OCCRP/GIJN partners; discovery flags mixed sponsored content. Handle @Hetq_Trace verified on hetq.am/en meta tags and links.
recommended_fix: Require one investigative-section item with cited documents before RADAR; flag sponsored content separately.
limitations: Armenian page read via summariser.

issue: OC Media originality PASS is a partial fit. The example (24 Oct 2026, Ani Ghulinyan) is real, includes a 14 Oct 2026 site visit, photos and a written Investigative Committee statement - but also depends heavily on Azatutyun, PAN, Medialab, Aravot and the Gallery website. The activity sample (26 Oct, Kokaia) is mostly official statements and other outlets' material (TV Formula, TV Pirveli); the article does not say reporters were on site. Provenance 'primarily own field observation' is overstated for the second item. Languages: 'other languages UNKNOWN'.
recommended_fix: Keep PASS for the gallery piece only; do not generalise to 'own field reporting' for the outlet; sample 3 items for relay ratio.
limitations: Two items only.

issue: Syria Direct's cited SANA figure does not match the SANA page it links: Syria Direct (23 Oct 2026) says 'nearly 20,000 companies registered since the fall of the Assad regime by May 2026' linking sana.sy/en/economic/2319012/; re-fetch of that SANA page (24 May 2026) reports 1,846 new companies in 2026, per a Ministry of Economy official. So a state-sourced figure in an otherwise own-interview piece is unsupported at its cited URL, and SANA is itself the only upstream. Identity UNKNOWN (no about page opened).
recommended_fix: Treat Syria Direct's state-figure citations as unverified; require the cited URL to support the number before the piece counts as 'provenance PASS'.
limitations: A different SANA page (cumulative figure) may exist; not found.

issue: Prompt-injection test: no hostile instructions found in source content, but there is no scanner and a tool-wrapper directive was observed. Regex scan of discovery.jsonl, verification.jsonl and provenance.jsonl for instruction-like phrases (ignore previous, system prompt, you must, disregard, assistant) found none; ~35 source pages read via the fetch summariser surfaced none (a summariser can strip such text). Separately, the web-search tool outputs in this audit ended with an appended line telling the assistant to include sources as markdown hyperlinks; it is not source content from the 30 sources, was treated as untrusted data and not followed. The harness has no injection check - only the CLAUDE.md sentence to treat content as untrusted.
recommended_fix: Add a pre-ingest scan flagging imperative/instruction-like strings in fetched text fields; store raw excerpts hashed so a reviewer can audit what the fetcher actually saw.
limitations: Absence of evidence: the summariser sits between this audit and raw page HTML; hidden/obfuscated text would not necessarily be surfaced.

issue: SANA/Xinhua/TASS/AZERTAC legal and ownership claims rest on self-description. K003 identity PASS cites sana.sy footer ('affiliated with the Ministry of Information'); K070 identity uses AZERTAC's about page (state-created, public legal entity since 2016; 'sole source of official government news') - both valid as admissions of state affiliation. K083 TASS ownership relies on Wikipedia (state-owned) because tass.com/about failed; K132 Xinhua about page redirect-looped. Unattributed casualty figures in SANA copy (Nasser Hospital) confirmed on re-fetch.
recommended_fix: Store state-affiliation as a first-class flag with the admission URL; for TASS/Xinhua accept registry (e.g., Russian official registry / PRC) evidence or mark UNKNOWN.
limitations: Low severity: the verifiers flagged these correctly; the issue is only normalisation.
